findings.reason: the refusal must read the recorded `dispatch_options` value (or be applied at the CLI boundary) rather than only CLI-threaded parameters, or every queued, resumed and re-resolved brief run is refused at plan time.
findings.text: §3 says `plan_dispatch` is called by only two callers, `dispatch()` for the launch and the dry-run branch, and that threading the two values through them covers the refusal; but `plan_dispatch` has eight production callers (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:687`, `:1047`, `:1177`, `:1233`, `:1670`, `:2009`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1713`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2924`), and the admission launch of a queued request is `dispatch()` called from `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:418` with `dispatch_options=options` and no plan-link parameter, while the lane-change path at `dispatch_sessions.py:1713` and the re-resolve paths at `dispatch.py:2009` and `:687` rebuild the node from the record with no value at all. A brief executable run dispatched after this change is stored with the link in `dispatch_options`, then refused when the admit service launches it, when it is lane-changed, and when its budget fallback re-resolves; a brief run dispatched before this change (which §3 keeps landing for, explicitly) is refused on any of those paths too, and none of the six done-when cases exercises a launch from the queue or a re-resolved node.

findings.reason: adding an ordering edge between §3 and §5 prevents two workers from writing the same files, which the parallel-safety rule forbids.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares `s3: [a-refusal-comes-before-the-work#s2]` and `s5: [a-refusal-comes-before-the-work#s2]` only, while §3's and §5's write paths both include `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py`, so once §2 lands the coordinator can dispatch §3 and §5 concurrently onto the same two files.

response_events.note: §3 is narrowed to the one entry a coordinator meets: the crew dispatch CLI (crew_dispatch_commands.py) refuses and records there, before plan_dispatch. plan_dispatch's other callers, which re-dispatch, re-resolve, change lane or admit a run already dispatched, neither refuse nor carry the value, and the landing discharge falls back to the landing flags for a run without one. dispatch.py and dispatch_plan.py leave its write paths.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited file and line resolves: `crew_dispatch_commands.py:1451`/`:1157`/`:1159`/`:1861`/`:2179`, `evidence.py:277`, `promotion_checks.py:1769` (`_require_brief_owner`), `dispatch.py:1670`, the dry-run `plan_dispatch` call at `crew_dispatch_commands.py:1917`, and `dispatch_batch.py:362-375`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — all six cases are observable assertions and each of the five controls names the mutation that makes the corresponding case red.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — logs are written under the run directory, a durable path that survives the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test and every named symbol are mechanism-named; no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers are introduced.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3 says the values are threaded from the CLI through "both of its callers", but `plan_dispatch` has eight production call sites and the four that re-resolve a node (a queued request's admission launch, a lane change, a budget fallback and an oversized-context reroute) pass neither value, so the new refusal fires on brief runs the plan says must keep working.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable: record the plan link or unplanned reason at dispatch and read it at landing.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §3 and §5 both declare `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` as write paths, but `plan-section-depends-on` orders each only after §2, so nothing sequences §3 against §5.
